summary: The unsafe flow passes network-sourced data (read from a socket in badSource()) directly as the format string argument to System.out.printf in the bad() entry point, allowing uncontrolled format directives (CWE-134). The fix uses a constant "%s" format string and passes the untrusted data as a value argument, so the data is printed literally without being interpreted as format specifiers. This preserves the feature (the data is still printed) while neutralizing the format-string vulnerability.
